  "foreword": [
    "This student handbook is specifically initiated and designed for young men and women who look forward to acquiring quality applied sciences and technology education from Bicol State College of Applied Sciences and Technology.",
    "The regulations in this Student Handbook shall apply to all undergraduate and graduate students who are enrolled in this College. To maintain discipline and orderliness, conserve the fair name of the College, and actualize its Mission, Vision and Core Values, students shall agree to abide by these same regulations and conduct themselves with good demeanor upon admission to this institution.",
    "Apart from serving as a ready reference material, this student handbook offers a peek into the workings of the BISCAST community and the place of the knowledge seekers in our educational mainstream.",
    "The administrative authority of the College is vested in the President of the institution. Conforming to the spirit of the ongoing policies set by the academic community, the continued attendance of any student in BISCAST subjects him or her to this authority.",
    "This 2025 student handbook, duly approved by the BISCAST Board of Trustees on May 14, 2025, under BOT Res. No. 30 s. 2025 reflects the school policies promulgated and implemented since the publication of the 2015 student handbook and the revisions of some statements for clarity and accuracy. Thus, this edition replaces the 2015 student handbook approved on July 15, 2015, under BOT Res. No. 104 s. 2015."
  ],

      "part_number": "PART I",
      "title": "THE COLLEGE",
      "sections": [
        {
          "section_number": "1",
          "title": "Brief History of BISCAST",
          "paragraphs": [
            "The school's history traces its humble beginnings in 1911, when it started as the Camarines Sur Trade School (CSTS). Mr. Pedro Hidalgo, the school administrator, organized trade courses in the intermediate level, offering carpentry, drawing, and trade arts. Classes were first held at the library hall of the Camarines Sur High School. In 1924, it started offering vocational courses at the Secondary level under the administration of Mr. Doroteo Federis.",
            "In November 1925, the first permanent school building was constructed, the Gabaldon building, on its 25,699-sq.m school site donated by the provincial government. This building still exists and is considered as the school's historical landmark. Woodworking courses were also introduced during the term of Mr. Cornelio Casaclang as Principal.",
            "At the outbreak of World War II, the school principal was Mr. Romulo Y. Mendoza. In 1945, the school reopened under Mrs. Primitiva Obias as Officer-in-Charge until the reassignment of Mr. Cornelio Casaclang. Auto-mechanics, Building Construction, Furniture and Cabinet Making were offered. In 1948, during the administration of Oligario Lenon, girls' trades courses in Dressmaking, Cosmetology, and Food Trades were offered, along with the construction of buildings and shops.",
            "House Bill No. 2919 (R.A. 825), sponsored by Congressman Emilio Tible and approved on August 15, 1952, nationalized and renamed Camarines Sur National School of Arts and Trades (CSNSAT). Mr. Manuel T. Espinosa became its first superintendent. In 1954, the two-year post-secondary trade technical education was offered.",
            "Upon its conversion to a full-fledged college under R.A. No. 5056, sponsored by Cong. Ramon H. Felipe, Jr. on June 17, 1967, the CSNSAT was converted into a college and renamed Bicol College of Arts and Trades (BCAT). It was authorized to offer courses like the Bachelor of Science in Industrial Education (BSIE). Before it formally assumed its name as BCAT, it was known as Camarines Sur National College of Arts and Trades (CSNCAT) until the mid-1980s, when it adopted its name BCAT.",
            "The tertiary level was expanded to cover other fields of trade technical education; thus, the Bachelor of Science in Industrial Technology (BSIT) was opened in 1977. Under the Technical-Vocational Education Project (TVEP), it was selected as one of the pilot Technician Education Institutes (TEI) for Region V by the Ministry of Education, Culture, and Sports (MECS). The project's education component was operationalized in the school year 1984-1985 by offering the two-year Diploma in Industrial Technician (DIT) curriculum with four major fields of specialization: Automotive, Mechanical, Electrical, and Refrigeration and Air Conditioning technologies.",
            "In 1984, Dr. Pacita S. Yorobe temporarily headed the school. Five months later, on April 1, 1985, Superintendent Augusto R. Nieves took over—the second alumnus to achieve such status. In 1988, by DECS Order No. 39, s. 1988, the Teacher Education component was expanded through the offering of the Bachelor of Secondary Education (BSEd), major in Technology and Home Economics (THE), Mathematics, English, and Physics; and Bachelor of Science in Elementary Education (BEEd) with the area of specialization in Home Economics and Livelihood Education (HELE).",
            "Under the administration of Mr. Honesto T. Aguilar, the 5th School Superintendent, BCAT started its offering of engineering courses, namely: Electrical Engineering (BSEE), Electronics and Communications Engineering (BSECE), Mechanical Engineering (BSME), and Bachelor of Science in Architecture (BSA). The institution had its first Engineering and Architecture graduates in March of 2001 and has steadily produced board passers and topnotchers until now.",
            "BCAT continued its bid for excellence in technology and teacher education under Mr. Pedro F. Moreno, the 6th Superintendent of the College. It remained undefeated during the annual Skills Olympics among TECHVOC schools in the Region. Its students maintained its dominance in the FFP-FAHP contests for high school students.",
            "In December 2000, pursuant to Republic Act 8760, on the integration of CHED-Supervised Institutions (CSIs) to State Universities and Colleges (SUCs), the Bicol College of Arts and Trades was integrated into the Camarines Sur Polytechnic Colleges (CSPC) in Nabua, Camarines Sur, with Dr. Lourdes B. Laniog as its President and Dr. Amparo A. Nieves as the Campus Director in the Naga Campus. On July 1, 2002, Dr. Monsito G. Ilarde was appointed President of CSPC. Dr. Alejandro R. Cortez was the new Campus Director until October 2003, when the position was reverted to Dr. Nieves until her retirement in 2006. Pursuant to CSPC Board of Trustees Resolution No. 00-044, the former BCAT was named CSPC - Naga Campus.",
            "Under the presidency of Dr. Dulce F. Atian in 2010, the Naga Campus was entrusted under the care of Dr. Richard H. Cordial as Campus Director from May 2010 to May 2012 and then as Campus Administrator until November 2012.",
            "On October 19, 2012, under the sponsorship of Cong. Luis R. Villafuerte of the 3rd District of Camarines Sur, Pres. Benigno Aquino III signed the passage of RA 10231, formally separating the school from CSPC and naming it the Bicol State College of Applied Sciences and Technology (BISCAST) with its first President, Dr. Richard H. Cordial. With its impressive new moniker, the institution is given its new mandate.",
            "Establishing BISCAST as an independent state college has paved the way to rapid progress in institutionalizing quality assurance systems, strengthening its research capabilities, and modernizing its facilities.",
            "In June 2020, the Congress approved House Bill 6858 filed by Rep. Luis Raymund F. Villafuerte, Jr. of the 2nd District of Camarines Sur, converting BISCAST from being a state college to a state university, which shall be named the Southeast Asian University of Technology (SEAUTech).",
            "In 2021, just a year after the world witnessed the impact of the pandemic, the institution transitioned to its new leadership in March, welcoming the second SUC President, Dr. Alex H. Navarroza, by virtue of the CHED Memorandum No. 3 Series of 2001, otherwise known as the Implementing Rules & Regulations of Republic Act 8292.",
            "Several months after Dr. Navarroza was appointed President, the bill converting BISCAST to SEAUTech was signed into law through RA 11585. On September 10, 2021, President Rodrigo R. Duterte presented a copy of the said law to Dr. Navarroza at the Malacañang Palace.",
            "The then CSNCAT, the BCAT, the CSPC-Naga Campus, now BISCAST, and soon SEAUTech, has survived through over 114 years as an institution of learning and served generations of Bicolanos, leading young men and women who have passed through its portals as productive citizens or community leaders.",
            "In this time of great volatility, uncertainty, complexity, and ambiguity, the College continues to be steadfast and resilient in putting its stakeholders at the core of its mission while preparing for its ultimate destination as a full-fledged smart, future-proof, technopreneurial, green, and healthy Southeast Asian University of Technology."
          ]
        },

    {
      "part_number": "PART II",
      "title": "PHILOSOPHY AND OBJECTIVES",
      "sections": [
        {
          "section_number": "1",
          "title": "General Directives",
          "directives": [
            "1.1. Every student is regarded as an extension and reflection of the College. Hence, whether on or off the campus, they are expected to be a model of the highest norms of behavior befitting a true scholar, a future professional, and a respectable citizen.",
            "1.2. A student is expected to know the vision and mission of the College, the meaning of its logo, core values, and BISCAST Hymn.",
            "1.3. A student shall observe and respect the laws of the land, the standards of organized society, and the College's code of conduct, rules, and regulations.",
            "1.4. A student shall observe the guidelines on wearing the official school uniform and identification card (ID).",
            "1.5. Every student is encouraged to attend institution-sponsored activities."
          ]
        },
        {
          "section_number": "2",
          "title": "Social Norms",
          "introduction": "To ensure an atmosphere conducive to the pursuit of academic excellence and the formation of responsible and productive Filipino citizens, as well as to maintain the order necessary for the common good, the College prescribes the following norms:",
          "norms": [
            "2.1. Every student shall observe the usual norms of courtesy and etiquette in all interpersonal relationships with any College community member.",
            "2.2. Every student is expected to show respect and courtesy to all visitors on the campus.",
            "2.3. Every student is expected to cooperate in routine classroom procedures as well as to help in keeping classrooms and corridors clean, bearing in mind that:",
            "2.3.1. A decent, clean, and orderly classroom is conducive to learning;",
            "2.3.2. Chalkboard and pieces of chalk are for instructional purposes only;",
            "2.3.3. Feet should be kept off furniture and walls; and",
            "2.3.4. Pieces of equipment are to be handled with responsible care and properly stored after use.",
            "2.4. Every student shall refrain from unruly conduct, unbecoming behavior, and actions that tend to disrupt and disturb the teaching-learning process. They should pass through corridors with minimal noise so as not to distract ongoing classes.",
            "2.5. Smoking any type of cigarette and the like is strictly prohibited inside the campus in observance of the Republic Act No. 8749 (known as the Philippine Clean Air Act) and Naga City Local Ordinance No. 2017-066.",
            "2.6. Students are encouraged to use school facilities for meetings, seminars, conferences, cultural presentations, athletic activities, and the like, but with prior permits from the authorities concerned.",
            "2.7. Any student who wishes to participate in any activity outside the campus as a representative of the College shall first secure a clearance from the Office of the Student Development Services, duly approved by the College President, and fully compliant with the requirements of CMO 63 s. 2017.",
            "2.8. Students who invite guests from outside are required to obtain prior approval from the Student Affairs Moderator and to submit a Visitor's List, indicating the names of campus visitors, the purpose of their visit, and their expected time of arrival.",
            "2.9. Students who intend to go on educational trips, excursions, and the like shall secure permission from the College Dean, Director of Student Development Services, recommended by the Vice President for Academic Affairs, and approved by the College President and shall present permits duly signed by their parents/guardians, itinerary of travel, budget proposal, and letter of confirmation from the agency/company to be visited, in compliance with CMO 63 s. 2017.",
            "2.10. Every student shall always wear the prescribed uniform properly, except during wash days, stormy weather, or when the Director of Student Development Services grants an exemption.",
            "2.11. In line with Republic Act No. 10121 ('Philippine Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Act of 2010'), all students are encouraged to participate in developing and implementing BISCAST disaster preparedness programs and actively engage in DRRM activities such as training sessions, drills, hazard reporting, and disaster awareness."
          ]
        }
      ]

      "title": "ADMISSION AND REGISTRATION",

        {
          "section_number": "1.0",
          "title": "BISCAST Policy Statement on Admission",
          "clauses": [
            "1.1 Accessibility to education is highly recognized by the College. No student shall be denied admission to the College because of age, gender, nationality, religious belief, disability, or political affiliation.",
            "1.2 The applicants must come from schools duly recognized by the government and pledge to abide by and comply with all the rules and regulations of the College upon Admission. Any violation thereof shall be sufficient cause for summary denial of admission or dismissal from the College.",
            "1.3 In recognition of the principles of equality and equity in providing access to education, the Admission Committee will set separate criteria to give priority treatment to disadvantaged students such as People with Disabilities, the Lumads, Muslims and other Indigenous people, Solo Parents and their children as mandated in the provisions of R.A. 10931, R.A. 7277, R.A. 8371, R.A. 11310, and R.A. 8972."
          ]
        },
        {
          "section_number": "2.0",
          "title": "Rules and Guidelines",
          "admission_procedures": [
            "2.1.1 All new students may apply for college admission at the Admission and Testing Center through the Student Information and Accounting System (SIAS) via https://icloudph.com/biscast/sias/. Application forms for admission can be downloaded at https://biscast.edu.ph/biscast-portal/.",
            "2.1.2 Transferees may be admitted if there are available slots, and they satisfy the admission and residency requirements. (2.1.2.1: Remaining units must be 50% or above; 2.1.2.2: Taken subjects are validated for accreditation; 2.1.2.3: Unequivalent or low-grade subjects shall be repeated).",
            "2.1.3 Second-degree students may be admitted provided there are available slots, and they abide by the policy that only 50% of the total units earned shall be credited. They will not enjoy free tuition as stipulated in R.A. 10931.",
            "2.1.6 Standardized College Admission Tests (OLSAT and DAT) are administered to all applicants.",
            "2.1.7 During instances that will demand particular measures on public health, BISCAST shall firmly implement DOH standard health protocols.",
            "2.1.8 Admission Test criteria weights: IQ Test (30%), Aptitude Test (70%).",
            "2.2.1 (Special Case) If the College Admission Test is waived or cancelled due to unforeseen events (i.e. health crisis, force majeure), first-year applicants shall be evaluated through the Admission Scoring Criteria for the first screening, and an interview and/or special exam for the second screening."

          "title": "Deferment of Enrollment",
          "verbatim_text": "New students who, for a valid reason, cannot enroll during the semester applied for may apply for Deferment of Enrollment at the Registrar's Office. The maximum period for deferment is only one school year."
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "part_number": "PART V",
      "title": "ACADEMIC DELINQUENCY",
      "sections": [
        {
          "section_number": "1.0",
          "title": "Class Attendance and Leave of Absence",
          "general_policy": "All students shall be obliged to attend classes punctually and regularly. Leave of absence shall be filed by the student when they will be absent for an extended period due to illness or other justifiable reasons.",
          "subsections": [
            {
              "id": "1.1",
              "title": "Allowable Absences",
              "rule": "Students shall be allowed to attend class and not be dropped, provided that the absences are valid and do not exceed 20% of the prescribed class hours for the semester. If the absences are incurred in three (3) consecutive class days or five (5) accumulated days, the faculty concerned shall refer the student to the class adviser for formal notification to the parents or guardian. Similarly, the adviser may conduct a home visit, investigation, or follow-up to identify and address the issue of absences. If the student continues to be absent even after the intervention made by the adviser, the case shall be appropriately referred to the Guidance Office using the Student Referral Form."
            },
            {
              "id": "1.2",
              "title": "Excused Absences",
              "rule": "Absences incurred due to activities authorized by the College shall be considered excused, such as attendance to athletic meets, conferences, and other academic-related activities, and other valid reasons as determined by the Office of the Student Development Services. Excuses are for time lost only. All work covered by the class during the absence shall be made up within the term by the student concerned. The time lost by late enrollment shall be considered time lost by absence and not excused."
            },
            {
              "id": "1.3",
              "title": "Medical Certificate",
              "rule": "Students absent from classes due to illness must obtain a medical certificate from the College Health Services. Illnesses attended elsewhere shall be reported to the Health Service Office within three days after the absences have been incurred, and a medical certificate will be issued only after satisfactory evidence has been presented."
            },
            {
              "id": "1.4",
              "title": "Leave of Absence",
              "rule": "A leave of absence (LOA) is the non-enrollment of a student in the College. A student may request a LOA for up to one (1) school year for justifiable cause upon approval by the College concerned and notification of the Registrar's Office. The LOA shall not be deducted from the allowed residency when completing a degree. No LOA shall be granted after the Midterm examinations or within two weeks before the end of the summer term. If the inability of the student to continue is due to illness or similar justifiable reasons, the absence during this period shall be considered excused.",
              "legal_basis": "BOT Resolution No. 108, s. 2021"
            }
          ]
        },
        {
          "section_number": "2.0",
          "title": "Validation of Transfer Credentials",
          "general_policy": "All subjects taken from other schools by the transferee and second-degree students must undergo accreditation. Only those who meet the accreditation criteria will be credited by the college. The College offering the subject in coordination with the Registrar's Office shall determine the subjects to be accredited.",
          "subsections": [
            {
              "id": "2.1",
              "title": "Accreditation of Subjects",
              "criteria": [
                "1. The courses must have been taken within the last five (5) years at admission.",
                "2. The courses were taken from CHED-recognized higher education institutions.",
                "3. The course content and number of units are higher or the same as the College prescribes. In case the units are lacking, the subjects must be re-enrolled.",
                "4. The final grade is equivalent to 2.5 or better for undergraduate courses and 1.5 or better for graduate courses.",
                "5. The subjects earned must be toward a degree program.",
                "6. For transferees, the subjects must not exceed 50% of the total number of units prescribed in the curriculum and must be at least 75% if the student vies for honors upon graduation.",
                "7. For second-degree holders, the subjects must not exceed 50% of the total number of units prescribed for graduation.",
                "8. Courses taken with equivalency shall be subject to the policies and guidelines issued by CHED on course equivalency.",
                "9. Units earned in technical/vocational courses and high school shall not be credited toward a degree program.",
                "10. Validation/Accreditation should be completed within three (3) semesters from the date of admission to the institution."
              ]
            }
          ]
        },

            "3.1.2 Students who fail any major courses shall be allowed to re-take only once; otherwise, they shall be disqualified from the program.",
            "3.1.3 Probation status shall be lifted upon passing at least 75% of the enrolled courses during the term of probation.",
            "3.1.4 Probation period is given for only one (1) regular semester and is not applicable during the summer term.",
            "3.1.5 Placed on probation if deficiencies exceed 10% of total academic units (cumulative INC, dropping, and failing).",

            "3.3 Transferee limits: Disallowed to continue if they incur two failures or three (3) dropped subjects in their first term.",

            "1.2 College Scholarships": "Giving full free tuition to any undergraduate student who obtains a general weighted average of 1.5 or better with no INC or failing grades in one school year, provided that the student carries the prescribed academic load in the curriculum for a regular student; or 15 units for a working student, and provided further that the student is of good moral character.             "1.7 Student Assistantship": "The college provides opportunities to students who have the time and skills to work as student assistants in various offices and earn wages at a student rate.             "4.1 As College Representative. No student can participate in any outside activity, contest, play in a band, choir, conference, association, society, or group as a representative of the College or any of the recognized student organizations without the written authorization of the College President upon endorsement by the Office of Student Development Services. Participation in activities as an individual and not as a representative of the College is the student's responsibility; thus, they may not claim any award or recognition.",
            "4.2. Official Use of School Uniform in Public Places. Students wearing the school uniform in public should project themselves as persons with positive social conduct.",
            "4.3. Acts Which Put the College in Public Embarrassment. Acts that bring the name of the College into disrepute, such as a public and malicious imputation of a crime or a vice or defect, real or imaginary, or any act, omission, condition, status, or circumstance, tending to cause dishonor, discredit, or contempt to the name of the college, are strictly prohibited.",
            "4.4. Involvement in Street Demonstrations or Rallies. The College is not responsible for the actions of students who, on their own, without regard for the existing law, and despite awareness of possible grave punitive sanctions, shall engage in such activities, actively or passively.       "title": "STUDENT'S WELFARE AND SERVICES",
      "sections": [
        {
          "section_number": "1.0",
          "title": "Student Affairs and Services (SAS)",
          "services": {
            "1.1 Information and Orientation Services": "Refers to informative activities to facilitate student adjustment to tertiary/higher education life. The institution shall make available information materials on institutional mission, vision, goals, academic rules, student conduct and discipline, and other services. A regular comprehensive orientation program shall be held for new and continuing students.",
            "1.2 Library Services": "The college shall adopt an open library system for the students, providing for the library needs of every department. Rules: Library hours start from 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM daily (Mon-Fri) and Saturdays 8:00 AM to 12:00 PM. Library cards must be presented when borrowing. Home reading books may be borrowed for three (3) days and re-borrowed once. Overnight books borrowed from 4:00 PM must be returned before 9:00 AM next day. Late fee: Php 1.00 per hour. Stealing/destroying library property is strictly prohibited and considered a major disciplinary offense.",
            "1.3 Guidance Services": "A set of services using an integrated approach to developing well-functioning individuals primarily by helping them utilize their potential to the fullest. Includes: (1.3.1) Appraisal - gathering student data for cumulative records; (1.3.2) Counseling - individual and group gender-sensitive counseling with a counselor-student ratio of at least 1:1,000; (1.3.3) Follow-up - systematic monitoring of counseling activities; (1.3.4) Referral - coordination with external specialists.",
            "1.4 Career and Job Placement Services": "Refers to the assistance provided for vocational and occupational fitness and employment. The College shall maintain active networking with school, community, alumni, and employers to facilitate job opportunities.",
            "1.5 Student Handbook Development": "There shall be a mechanism to develop the student handbook, and updates shall be made into accessible formats (including but not limited to electronic, large print, media, braille, and sign language). It shall be reviewed and revised within five years after its issuance.",
            "1.6 Health Services": "Provides primary health care services administered by licensed medical, dental, and allied professionals. (1.6.1) Dental Services: assesses dental status, provides simple medical treatments, and refers complicated cases. (1.6.2) Medical Services: assesses health status, provides medical services for simple ailments, provides emergency care, and conducts simple diagnostic tests (e.g. sputum exam).",
            "1.7 Student Publication": "The College shall support the establishment of a student publication as provided in the Campus Journalism Act of 1991. The Collegian shall be the official newspaper of the students of BISCAST.",
            "1.8 Student Council/Government": "The official student council shall be the BISCAST Supreme Student Council (BISCAST-SSC). The President of BISCAST-SSC shall serve as the student representative on the BISCAST Board of Trustees (BOT).",
            "1.9 Student Organizations": "Students can form, join, and participate in campus organizations that promote physical, intellectual, moral, cultural, civic, spiritual, or political interests. All activities must be officially recognized by the SDS and supervised by the Student Affairs Moderator.",
            "1.10 Food Services": "The College shall set the criteria for food outlets' safety and sanitary conditions and periodically inspect outlets. Certificate to Operate must be displayed in a prominent area.",
            "1.11 Multi-Faith Services": "The College ensures respect for freedom of religion. The Multi-faith Office sponsors various programs, events, and religious/multi-religious activities (CMO 47 s. 2016).",
            "1.12 Safety and Security Services": "Maintains a safe and secure environment, buildings, and facilities compliant with government standards. Licensed security personnel shall ensure safety of students and their belongings.",
            "1.13 Student Discipline": "Formulates gender-sensitive rules and regulations in consultation with students and faculty, published in a student manual to define appropriate conduct and prescribe sanctions.",
            "1.14 Student Housing": "Provides assistance and/or a list of acceptable student dormitories and housing facilities that are safe, clean, affordable, and conducive to learning.",
            "1.15 Students with Special Needs": "Ensures academic accommodation is available to persons with disabilities and learners with special needs, providing life skills training and testing referrals.",
            "1.16 International Students Services": "Forges linkages and cooperative projects with international academic communities to provide academic advising, counseling, legal/immigration assistance, and emergency services."
          }
        }
      ]

            "1.1 Participation": "Offers programs under the Office of the Student Affairs Moderator to complement academic programs and promote holistic development.",
            "1.2 Integration to Minimize Interruption": "Student activities must be planned and assistance provided by advisers to minimize class interruption. All activities must be reflected in the organization's Action Plan.",
            "1.3 Administration of Activities": "Requests to hold campus activities (symposium, seminar, workshop) must be addressed to the Director of SDS not later than five (5) days before the scheduled activity.           "section_number": "1.3",
          "title": "Procedure on Offenses",
          "steps": [
            "1. An incident report shall be submitted to the SDS Office by an interested or aggrieved party stating the nature and circumstances of the offense;",
            "2. SDS Director shall inform the alleged student offender, in writing, of the following: i. The charges, circumstances, and evidence in the complaint; and ii. That they have 72 hours from receipt of the notice to answer the charges, in writing, and that failure to submit such a reply will be tantamount to waiver of the right to be heard;",
            "3. Along with the notice, SDS shall also provide the alleged offender with copies of the complaint and evidence thereof;",
            "4. SDS shall proceed to investigate the facts, assess the gravity of the offense, as well as the guilt and innocence of the offender;",
            "5. SDS shall impose an appropriate penalty if the case is assessed to be a minor offense;",
            "6. If the case involves the penalties of final warning status, suspension, dismissal, or expulsion, SDS shall refer the case and recommend such a penalty for a grave offense to the College Disciplinary Board (CDB) or the Committee on Decorum and Investigation (CODI), depending on the nature of the violation.",
            "7. Should there be a need for a full-blown inquiry, the CDB or CODI shall set a time, date, and venue to convene to determine the nature and degree of gravity of the offense and the appropriate intervention.",

            "9. The CDB or CODI shall determine the merits of the case, decide on the guilt or innocence, and determine to impose the SDS-recommended sanction or recommend another penalty;",
            "10. The CDB or CODI shall submit in writing, for the President's approval, its decision and recommended sanction;",
            "11. The SDS shall, in writing, communicate the President's decision to the student offender;",
            "12. Appeal may be made within five working days from receipt of the notice;",
            "13. The President's decision on appeal shall be final and executory."

          "title": "Separability Clauses",
          "verbatim_text": "Should any provisions, section, or part of this Student Handbook be declared by any competent authorities as invalid, the remaining provisions, sections, or parts thereof remain in full force and effect.           "title": "Transitory Provision",
          "verbatim_text": "This Student Handbook will continue using the institution's name - Bicol State College of Applied Sciences and Technology until the full approval and transition to Southeast Asian University of Technology under RA 11585."
        },
        {
          "section_number": "3",
          "title": "Amendments and Revisions",
          "verbatim_text": "Subsequent editions of the Student Handbook that incorporate updates arising from recently approved institutional policies—provided these do not constitute major revisions to existing provisions, as determined by the Academic Council Committee on Student Affairs and Services—shall only require the approval of the Academic Council. Students will be notified of significant updates through official communication channels within one month after release. On the other hand, significant revisions to the Student Handbook, defined as substantial changes affecting student rights, responsibilities, or institutional policies, shall require review and recommendation by the Academic Council Committee on Student Affairs and Services, consultation with key stakeholders (including student representatives), and final approval by the Board of Trustees."
